_comment: The core-declared file form for chimera's project wizard: a PlayStation 2 project is one disc or one executable, and whatever the machine is to start with already written on its cards. The bios is not here - it is firmware, which the frontend resolves once and remembers, rather than something a project carries.

slots.title: Disc or program
slots.help: What the machine runs. Usually a DVD or CD image: a plain .iso or .bin (2048- or 2352-byte sectors, with or without a .cue beside it), or a compressed one - .chd, .cso, .zso, .gz. It can also be a PS2 EXECUTABLE (.elf), which is what homebrew and test programs ship as: the tray stays empty and the machine is handed the program to run instead, exactly as it would run a disc's own boot file. What decides is the file's first four bytes, not its name, so an executable called anything still boots. A project with no file at all is a console sitting at its own browser, which is a machine worth booting - but the wizard asks for one, because a movie is usually of a game.

slots.title: Save data
slots.help: What the machine starts with already saved: memory cards, and the console's own NVRAM. These are the files Emulator > Export Save Data... writes, put back under the same names - memcard1.ps2, memcard2.ps2, bios.nvm - so a run can continue from where another left off. Each is mounted read-only and pinned by hash, and the movie cites it, so a movie that starts from a saved game is as reproducible as one that starts from a blank card. Leave it empty and the machine boots with blank cards, which is a new console.
